title: Missing nonReentrant on batchMint combined with balanceOf-driven nudge payout exposes the contract to ERC777/rebasing/fee-on-transfer hazards
rootCause: `batchMint` is not protected by a `nonReentrant` modifier. Sub-issues involving exotic ERC20 tokens (rebasing, fee-on-transfer, ERC777, double-entry-point) are excluded by C4 known-invalid patterns.
consolidatedDescription:
Surviving substance after sanitization: missing OpenZeppelin `ReentrancyGuard` on `batchMint`. Defense-in-depth recommendation only - no demonstrated H/M exploit against tokens the project actually supports (standard ERC20s like phUSD, USDC). The ERC777 / rebasing / FoT vectors are filtered by the project's known-invalid list.

Adding `nonReentrant` is a one-line cheap hardening that closes the theoretical reentrancy class regardless of the deployed nudge token, and is consistent with the project's stated preference for OpenZeppelin standard primitives (CLAUDE.md).
exploitScenarioCanonical: Not applicable for standard ERC20 tokens. Theoretical: if a token with a transfer hook (ERC777) were ever configured as `nudgePaymentToken`, a recipient contract could re-enter `batchMint` from `tokensReceived`. The project's known-invalid list excludes this class.
unionOfMitigations: Add OpenZeppelin `ReentrancyGuard` and apply `nonReentrant` to `batchMint`. One-line defense-in-depth.
Document explicitly in NatSpec that `nudgePaymentToken` MUST be a standard non-rebasing, non-fee-on-transfer, non-hooked ERC20 (USDC, DAI, etc.).
preservedDetails: Sanitizer dropped sub-issues (B), (C), (D) per C4 known-invalid (exotic ERC20s).

sanitization.rationale: C4 known-invalid patterns explicitly exclude non-standard ERC-20 tokens (fee-on-transfer, rebasing, ERC777 hooks, double-entry-point) unless explicitly in scope. Sub-issues (B) rebasing, (C) fee-on-transfer event mismatch, and (D) double-entry-point all fall under that exclusion and should be DROPPED from this finding. The surviving substance is sub-issue (A): missing nonReentrant on batchMint as defense-in-depth. That alone does not have a demonstrated H/M exploit path against any token the project actually supports - it is best framed as a QA recommendation to add ReentrancyGuard.
sanitization.surviving_scope: Add nonReentrant to batchMint as defense-in-depth (QA).

classification.justification: QA-grade defense-in-depth recommendation. No demonstrated H/M exploit path against the standard ERC20s the project supports (phUSD, USDC). Adding `nonReentrant` is a one-line cheap hardening consistent with the project's stated preference for OpenZeppelin primitives.
guardrails_observed: Project's known-invalid list excludes non-standard ERC20s, filtering the rebasing/FoT/ERC777 vectors.
The nudge payout `safeTransfer` happens AFTER the approval revoke and AFTER the inner mint loop, so the only state visible from a hooked-recipient re-entry is post-loop state.
